# Libraries 
```{r}
# spatial data science
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(units)

# Data
library(AOI)

# Visualization
library(gghighlight)
library(ggrepel)
library(knitr)
library(dplyr)
library(flextable)
```

# Question 1
```{r}
#1.1 
eqdc <- '+proj=eqdc +lat_0=40 +lon_0=-96 +lat_1=20 +lat_2=60 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=NAD83 +units=m +no_defs'

#1.2 
remotes::install_github("mikejohnson51/AOI")
states <- aoi_get(state = 'conus')
states <- st_transform(states, crs = eqdc)

#1.3 
countries <- aoi_get(country = c("MX", "CA", "USA"))
sf::st_crs(countries)
countries <- st_transform(countries, crs = eqdc)

#1.4 
library(readr)
uscities <- read_csv("data/uscities_data/uscities.csv")
uscities_sf <- st_as_sf(uscities, 
                        coords = c("lng", "lat"),  
                        crs = 4326)
# Remove cities in Alaska, Hawaii, and Puerto Rico
uscities_sf_filtered <- uscities_sf %>%
  filter(!state_name %in% c("Alaska", "Hawaii", "Puerto Rico"))
uscities_sf_filtered <- st_transform(uscities_sf_filtered, crs = eqdc)
```

# Question 2
```{r}
##2.1 Distance to U.S. Border (km0)
usa_union <- st_union(states) #Combine    
usa_border <- st_boundary(usa_union)

uscities_sf_filtered$distance_to_border_km <- st_distance(uscities_sf_filtered, usa_border) %>%
  as.numeric() / 1000 
#Five farthest cities 
farthest_cities <- uscities_sf_filtered %>%
  arrange(desc(distance_to_border_km)) %>%
  select(city, state_name, distance_to_border_km) %>%
  slice(1:5) %>%
  mutate(distance_to_border_km = round(distance_to_border_km, 2))

#Table 
farthest_table_df <- farthest_cities %>%
  st_drop_geometry()
farthest_table <- flextable(farthest_table_df) %>%
  set_header_labels(
    city = "City",
    state_name = "State",
    distance_to_border_km = "Distance to Border (km)")%>%
  autofit()
print(farthest_table)
```


```{r}
##2.2 Distance to States (km)
state_boundaries <- st_boundary(states) #combine
combined_state_lines <- st_union(state_boundaries)

#Calculate distances
uscities_sf_filtered$distance_to_sb_km <- st_distance(uscities_sf_filtered, combined_state_lines)%>%
  as.numeric() / 1000 

#Five farthest cities
farthest_cities_sb <- uscities_sf_filtered %>%
  arrange(desc(distance_to_sb_km)) %>%
  select(city, state_name, distance_to_sb_km) %>%
  slice(1:5) %>%
  mutate(distance_to_sb_km = round(distance_to_sb_km, 2))

#Table
farthest_table_sb <- farthest_cities_sb %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  flextable() %>%
  set_header_labels(
    city = "City",
    state_name = "State",
    distance_to_sb_km = "Distance to State Border (km)") %>%
  autofit()
print(farthest_table_sb)
```

# Question 3
```{r}
##3.1 Plot for largest 10 cities 
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggrepel)

# Extract the top 10 cities by population
top_10_cities <- uscities_sf_filtered %>%
  arrange(desc(population)) %>%
  slice(1:10)

# Make plot
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countries, fill = "lightgray", color = "white", lwd = 0.2) +
  
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, color = "black", size = 1, lty = 1) +
  
 ggrepel::geom_label_repel(data = top_10_cities,
                            aes(x = st_coordinates(top_10_cities)[,1], 
                                y = st_coordinates(top_10_cities)[,2],
                                label = city),
                            size = 2, 
                            max.overlaps = Inf, 
                            box.padding = 0.5,  
                            nudge_y = 0.1,      
                            nudge_x = 0.1,      
                            segment.size = 0.5, 
                            segment.color = "black") +
  
  labs(title = "Top 10 Largest U.S. Cities by Population") + theme_minimal() +
 theme(axis.title = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none", 
        plot.title = element_text(size = 10))
```
```{r}
##3.2 Plot for city distance from national border
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = usa_border, color = "black", fill = NA, size = 1) +
  
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, color = "gray50", size = 0.4, lty = 2) +

  geom_sf(data = uscities_sf_filtered, 
          aes(color = distance_to_border_km), 
          size = 1.2, alpha = 0.7) +
  
  geom_sf(data = farthest_cities, 
          color = "red", 
          size = 3, shape = 21, fill = "yellow") +
  
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(data = farthest_cities,
                            aes(x = st_coordinates(farthest_cities)[,1], 
                                y = st_coordinates(farthest_cities)[,2],
                                label = city),
                            size = 2.5,
                            box.padding = 0.4,
                            nudge_y = 0.2,
                            segment.size = 0.4,
                            segment.color = "black") +
  
  coord_sf(xlim = st_bbox(states)[c("xmin", "xmax")],
           ylim = st_bbox(states)[c("ymin", "ymax")],
           expand = FALSE) +
  
  labs(title = "U.S. Cities Distance to National Border",
       subtitle = "Top 5 Farthest Cities from the Border",
       caption = "Distance measured in kilometers",
       color = "Distance to Border (km)") +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.25, "cm"),
    legend.key.width = unit(0.3, "cm"),
    legend.spacing.y = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10), plot.caption = element_text(size = 6))
```

```{r}
##3.4 Equidistant boundary from Mexico and Canada 
# Make new column
uscities_sf_filtered$abs_diff_can_mex <- abs(
  uscities_sf_filtered$distance_to_canada_border_km - 
  uscities_sf_filtered$distance_to_mexico_border_km)

# Filter for equidistant cities
zone_cities <- uscities_sf_filtered %>%
  filter(abs_diff_can_mex < 50)

# Top 5 most populus 
top5_zone <- zone_cities %>%
  arrange(desc(population)) %>%
  slice(1:5)

# Plot with gghighlight
library(gghighlight)
ggplot(data = uscities_sf_filtered) +
  geom_sf(aes(color = abs_diff_can_mex), size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  
  # Highlight only cities near equidistant zone
  gghighlight(abs_diff_can_mex < 50, label_key = city, use_direct_label = FALSE) +
  
  # Label top 5 populous cities in the zone
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(data = top5_zone,
                            aes(x = st_coordinates(top5_zone)[,1],
                                y = st_coordinates(top5_zone)[,2],
                                label = city),
                            size = 2.5,
                            box.padding = 0.4,
                            segment.size = 0.4) +
  
  # Add national border and state outlines
  geom_sf(data = usa_border, color = "black", fill = NA, size = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, color = "gray60", size = 0.4, lty = 2) +
  
  coord_sf(xlim = st_bbox(states)[c("xmin", "xmax")],
           ylim = st_bbox(states)[c("ymin", "ymax")],
           expand = FALSE) +
  
  labs(title = "Cities Equidistant from Canadian and Mexican Borders",
       subtitle = "Top 5 most populous cities in this zone are labeled",
       color = "Abs. Distance Diff (km)",
       caption = "Highlighted cities are within ~50 km difference in border distances") +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.25, "cm"),
    legend.key.width = unit(0.3, "cm"),
    legend.spacing.y = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(), plot.title = element_text(size = 12), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9), plot.caption = element_text(size = 6))

```

# Question 4
```{r}
##4.1 Quantifying Border Zone
# Filter cities within 160 km (100 miles) from the U.S. border
border_zone_cities <- uscities_sf_filtered %>%
  filter(distance_to_border_km <= 160)

# Count the number of cities within the 100-mile zone
num_cities_in_zone <- nrow(border_zone_cities)
num_cities_in_zone

# Sum the population of cities within the border zone
total_population_in_zone <- sum(border_zone_cities$population, na.rm = TRUE)
total_population_in_zone

# Total U.S. population estimate
total_us_population <- 330000000

# Calculate percentage of total U.S. population in this zone
percentage_population_in_zone <- (total_population_in_zone / total_us_population) * 100
percentage_population_in_zone

# Flextable to organize info
quantify_border <- data.frame(
  "Metric" = c("Number of Cities", "Total Population in Zone", 
              "Percentage of U.S. Population in Zone", "Does it Match the ACLU Estimate?"),
  "Value" = c(num_cities_in_zone, total_population_in_zone, 
              round(percentage_population_in_zone, 2), "Yes"))

quantify_border <- flextable(quantify_border) %>%
  set_header_labels(
    Metric = "Metric",
    Value = "Value"
  ) %>%
  autofit()
print(quantify_border)

```

```{r}
##4.2 Mapping Border Zone
# Identify the 10 most populous cities within the 100-mile zone
top_10_border_zone <- border_zone_cities %>%
  arrange(desc(population)) %>%
  slice(1:10)

# Plot
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, color = "gray70", lwd = 0.5) +
  
  # Use distance to border for color
  geom_sf(data = border_zone_cities, aes(color = distance_to_border_km), size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  
  # Highlight all cities in the filtered dataset (all are within 100 miles)
  gghighlight::gghighlight(TRUE, use_direct_label = FALSE) +
  
  # Gradient: darker red = closer to border
  scale_color_gradient(low = "darkred", high = "orange", name = "Distance to Border (km)") +
  
  # Label top 10 most populous cities
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
    data = top_10_border_zone,
    aes(x = st_coordinates(top_10_border_zone)[, 1],
        y = st_coordinates(top_10_border_zone)[, 2],
        label = city),
    size = 2, box.padding = 0.3, max.overlaps = 10) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.25, "cm"),
    legend.key.width = unit(0.3, "cm"),
    legend.spacing.y = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 13)) +
  labs(
    title = "Map of Border Zone (Within 100 Miles)")
```

```{r}
##4.3 Most Populous city in Each State in Zone
# Most populous city in each state within zone
most_populous_by_state <- border_zone_cities %>%
  group_by(state_name) %>%
  filter(population == max(population, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Plot
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, color = "gray70", lwd = 0.5) +
  
  # Use distance to border for color
  geom_sf(data = border_zone_cities, aes(color = distance_to_border_km), size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  
  # Highlight all cities in the filtered dataset (all are within 100 miles)
  gghighlight::gghighlight(TRUE, use_direct_label = FALSE) +
  
  # Gradient: darker red = closer to border
  scale_color_gradient(low = "darkred", high = "orange", name = "Distance to Border (km)") +
  
 ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
  data = most_populous_by_state,
  aes(x = st_coordinates(most_populous_by_state)[, 1],
      y = st_coordinates(most_populous_by_state)[, 2],
      label = city),
  size = 1.45,           
  box.padding = 0.2,
  max.overlaps = Inf) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.25, "cm"),
    legend.key.width = unit(0.3, "cm"),
    legend.spacing.y = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 13)) +
  labs(
    title = "Map of Border Zone (Within 100 Miles)",
    subtitle = "Labeled: Most populous city in each state within the zone")
```
